alessandro@anatrini.com | anatrini.com

Practice

Alessandro Anatrini is a composer, computational artist, and researcher. Through worldbuilding and simulation practices, he develops computational systems in which space, sound, and image evolve adaptively. Reworking forms from the past—Renaissance architectures, ancient cartographies, maps of premodern thought—he shapes immersive environments where image and sound articulate as unstable phenomena, balanced between familiarity and disorientation.

Selected Works

Faulty Oracle

anatrini.com/works/faulty-oracle
2025

Interactive Generative Installation

Adaptive audiovisual installation conjuring gloriously unreliable divinatory machine. Visitors pose questions through body language—gestures, movements, postures which the system interprets, misreads, and wilfully transforms, delivering cryptic animated answers flickering between epiphany, nonsense, and hallucination.

Premiere: Occulture Conference, Malhalla, Berlin — October 23-26, 2025
Collaboration: Alessandro Aresta
Tools: TouchDesigner, Ableton Live, Python

Venerdì sera a letto presto

anatrini.com/works/venerdi-sera
2025

Friday night going to bed early — Audio-Video Fixed Media

Neural network-assisted domestic audiovisual wandering disrupts the ontological paradigm of "the couch as device of stasis." The camera becomes sentient interface generating a para-medieval bestiary, converting domestic space into diegetic ecology where corridor becomes nave and kitchen transforms into apse.

Premiere: Notte Europea della Ricerca, Piacenza — September 27, 2025
Duration: 7 minutes
Tools: Wavepilot, TouchDesigner, Ableton Live, Python

[ Reloaded ]

anatrini.com/works/reloaded
2024

Piano, Electronics, Toy Piano and Toy Instruments

Written for Non-Piano/Toy Piano Weekend Hamburg exploring the question: "How would have sounded a piano piece by Fausto Romitelli?" Taking cues from Romitelli's Amok Koma, conventional and toy instruments blend through live electronics without attempting literal translation.

Premiere: Resonanzraum, Hamburg — November 23, 2024
Duration: 9'50"
Performers: Jennifer Hymer, Bernhard Fograscher
Commission: Non-Piano/Toy Piano Weekend of Hamburg

Die Monsterfabrik

anatrini.com/works/monsterfabrik
2024

Audio-Video Fixed Media

Explores progressive transformation of Vivaldi's string music through iterative AI training. Each cycle produces models generating results increasingly distant from original as the neural network consumes its own output, creating baroque ghosts haunting contemporary computational processes.

Premiere: Ligeti Zentrum, Harburg — November 12, 2024
Duration: 10 minutes
Playback: 28.4 audio channels + video projection
Commission: Hamburg Open Online University (HOOU)

Sandy Island

anatrini.com/works/sandy
2022

Site-Specific Installation

Adaptive installation running continuously for 60 hours with 288 speakers arranged via Wavefield Synthesis. Named after the phantom island that appeared on maps for two centuries until proven non-existent in 2012, the work explores fallacious abilities to discern between representation and reality.

Premiere: Forum, HfMT Hamburg — December 1-3, 2022
Duration: 60 hours continuous operation
Playback: 288.0 channels (Wavefield Synthesis) + LED videowall
Collaboration: Lucas Xerxes, KLARA Janina Luckow, Alessandro Alessandri

Wunderkammer

anatrini.com/works/wunderkammer
2021

Interactive Generative Installation

Renaissance cabinet of curiosities transformed into intelligent sonic organism with finite life cycle of approximately 72 hours. Born with excellent adaptive capabilities, the neural network-based system gradually exhausts capacity for novelty, mirroring biological organisms from birth through senescence.

Premiere: Spazio Materia, Prato — May 27-30, 2021
Duration: ~72 hours continuous operation
Playback: 4.1 audio channels + neon light installation
Light Design: Jacopo Buono

Here Be Dragons

anatrini.com/works/intermezzo
2020

Interactive Generative Installation

Autonomous agent activating during concert intermissions, transforming dead time into living sonic territory. Operating as horror vacui—fear of emptiness—the system responds to ambient sound, producing unpredictable sonic responses that question whether silence exists in contemporary listening contexts.

Premiere: Künstlerhaus Faktor, Hamburg — October 22, 2020
Duration: Undefined (continuous/responsive)
Playback: 4.1 audio + projection canvas
Visual Design: KLARA Janina Luckow

Open Fields

anatrini.com/works/openfields
2019

Site-Specific Piece for 144 Musicians

144 musicians distributed across 900 meters of subterranean tunnel, 24 meters beneath the Elbe River. Hamburg's Alte Elbtunnel becomes resonance chamber with 72 musicians per tunnel at 3-meter intervals. Commissioned for the tunnel's reopening ceremony, transforming industrial infrastructure into immersive sonic environment.

Premiere: Alte Elbtunnel, Hamburg — May 25-26, 2019
Duration: 6 minutes
Spatial Config: Two parallel 450m tunnels, 24m underwater, 3m spacing
Score System: Rama Gottfried, Georg Hajdu (web-based distribution)

Il suo divertimento era di contare le stelle

anatrini.com/works/divertimento
2019

For Small Ensemble

Commissioned for Leopardi's 200th anniversary of "L'Infinito," the title translates as "His amusement was to count the stars." Extended silences punctuated by luminous gestures create sonic star chart where each note functions as point of light, isolated yet geometrically connected through invisible lines of temporal relationship.

Premiere: Le Torri dell'Acqua, Budrio — December 2, 2019
Duration: 2'30"
Instrumentation: Bass clarinet, electric guitar, piano, cello
Ensemble: FontanaMix Ensemble

Tap This

anatrini.com/works/tapthis
2019

For Two Electric Guitars

Explores electric guitar as melodic instrument and percussive interface through two-handed tapping technique. Extended techniques—harmonic tapping, percussive strikes, prepared strings, feedback manipulation—transform guitars into hybrid electroacoustic instruments seeking a third space between rock virtuosity and contemporary abstraction.

Premiere: Resonanzraum, Hamburg — December 7, 2019
Duration: 6 minutes
Dedicated to: Nicolas Haumann & Martin Donoso Vera
Commission: Hamburg Dialogues 2019

Unfamiliar Walks

anatrini.com/works/unfamiliar
2018

Interactive Installation

Generative sonic environment designed for hospital settings, confronting the paradox of creating engaging content that doesn't demand attention. Permanently installed in UKE Hamburg's waiting and emergency rooms, the autonomous system provides patients agency through touchscreen navigation, mitigating stress in environments characterized by anxiety and uncertainty.

Installation: UKE Hamburg — September 2018–ongoing
Duration: Continuous/undefined (autonomous generative system)
Playback: 4.0 (quadraphonic)
Project: Healing Soundscapes (HfMT Hamburg, UKE, MSH)

Fragile Territories

anatrini.com/works/fragile
2017

For Big Orchestra and Electronics

Constructs entire orchestral universe from single acoustic event: the oboe's tuning A at the work's beginning. This pitch—traditionally preparation before real music—becomes generative source, its spectral components analyzed and distributed across full orchestra exploring fragility in multiple dimensions.

Premiere: Laeiszhalle Miralles-Saal, Hamburg — June 22, 2017
Duration: 15 minutes
Instrumentation: Large orchestra + electronics
Commission: Hamburger Symphoniker

Esplorazione di una certa quantità d'acqua

anatrini.com/works/esplorazione
2017

For Ensemble

Transforms acoustic properties of water-filled glass into orchestral material. A goblet containing measured water volume becomes generative source, its resonances analyzed and orchestrated for nine instruments. Formal architecture mirrors physical resonance behavior, tracing trajectory from clarity to saturation.

Premiere: Arsonic, Mons — September 21, 2017
Duration: 7'30"
Instrumentation: Flute, bass clarinet, trombone, percussion, piano, electric guitar, violin, viola, cello
Commission: Ensemble Musiques Nouvelles

Forbite fantascienze

anatrini.com/works/forbite
2015

For Contrabassoon and Live Electronics

"Forbidden Science Fictions" explores contrabassoon's timbral extremes through real-time electronic augmentation. The instrument occupies liminal acoustic space—too low for melodic clarity, too present for pure bass function. Electronics function as both mirror and distortion lens distributed across 8.1 spatial configuration.

Premiere: Le Centquatre, Paris — June 27, 2015
Duration: 8 minutes
Dedicated to: Paul Riveaux (Ensemble Intercontemporain)
Commission: IRCAM Académie ManiFeste 2015
